children.translated_text: Because of the assault of the three kinds of suffering, there is a desire to know the means for removing them.
If it is said that this is pointless, since an evident means exists, no: because that means is neither certain nor final.
The means taught by revelation is like the evident one, for it is joined with impurity, decay, and excess.
Superior is the opposite of that, arising from discriminative knowledge of the manifest, the unmanifest, and the knower.
Root <s>prakṛti</s> is unevolved; the seven beginning with <s>mahat</s> are both <s>prakṛti</s> and evolutes.

children.text: ṣoḍaśakas tu vikāro na prakṛtir na vikṛtiḥ puruṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The group of sixteen is an evolute; <s>puruṣa</s> is neither <s>prakṛti</s> nor an evolute.
Perception, inference, and trustworthy speech are accepted, since all means of valid knowledge are established by them.
The means of valid knowledge is held to be threefold, for the establishment of what is to be known comes from valid knowledge.
Perception is ascertainment with respect to each object; inference is declared to be threefold.
It is preceded by the relation of sign and sign-bearer; trustworthy hearing is trustworthy speech.

children.text: sāmānyatas tu dṛṣṭād atīndriyāṇām pratītir anumānāt
children.translated_text: But from inference based on what is generally observed comes cognition of things beyond the senses.

children.text: tasmād api cāsiddham parokṣam āptāgamāt siddham ||
children.translated_text: And what is not established even by that, being remote, is established from trustworthy tradition.
Because of excessive distance, nearness, injury to the senses, instability of the mind,
subtlety, obstruction, being overpowered, and mingling with similar things,
its non-apprehension is due to subtlety, not to nonexistence; it is apprehended from its effect.

children.text: mahadādi tacca kāryam prakṛtivirūpaṃ sarūpaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: That effect is <s>mahat</s> and the rest, both unlike and like <s>prakṛti</s>.
Because the nonexistent cannot be produced, because a material cause is taken up, because not everything can arise from everything,
because what is capable produces what it can, and because of the nature of cause, the effect exists beforehand.

children.text: hetumad anityam avyāpi sakriyam anekam āśritaṃ liṅgam
children.translated_text: The manifest sign is caused, impermanent, non-pervasive, active, multiple, dependent,
composite, and subordinate; the unmanifest is the reverse.

children.text: triguṇam aviveki viṣayaḥ sāmānyam acetanaṃ prasavadharmi
children.translated_text: The manifest is constituted by the three <s>guṇas</s>, non-discriminating, an object, common, unconscious, and productive.

children.text: vyaktaṃ tathā pradhānaṃ tadviparītas tathā ca pumān ||
children.translated_text: So too is <s>pradhāna</s>; and <s>pumān</s>, the person, is the opposite of these.
The <s>guṇas</s> have the nature of pleasure, displeasure, and dejection, and serve illumination, activity, and restraint.
They also have functions of mutual overpowering, dependence, generation, pairing, and operation.

children.text: sattvaṃ laghu prakāśakam iṣṭam upaṣṭambhakaṃ calaṃ ca rajaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> is held to be light and illuminating; <s>rajas</s> is supporting and mobile.

children.text: guru varaṇakam eva tamaḥ pradīpavaccārthato vṛttiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Tamas</s> is heavy and concealing; their functioning is for a purpose, like a lamp.
The state of being non-discriminating and so on is established because of the three-<s>guṇa</s> nature, since the contrary of that is absent.
Because the effect has the nature of the qualities of the cause, the unmanifest too is established.
Because of the limited measure of differentiations, because of coordination, because activity proceeds from capacity,
because of the division between cause and effect, and because of the undividedness of the manifold universe,
there exists an unmanifest cause; it operates because it is three-<s>guṇa</s> and because of aggregation.
Its transformation is like water, according to the particular support of each respective <s>guṇa</s>.
Because composites exist for another's sake, because of the opposite of the three <s>guṇas</s> and the rest, because of a superintendent,
<s>Puruṣa</s> exists, because there is the condition of an enjoyer and because activity is for the sake of isolation.
Because births, deaths, and instruments are individually regulated, and because activity is not simultaneous,
the plurality of <s>puruṣas</s> is established, and also because of the opposition to the three-<s>guṇa</s> nature.

children.text: tasmācca viparyāsāt siddhaṃ sākṣitvam asya puruṣasya
children.translated_text: And from that contrast the witnesshood of this <s>puruṣa</s> is established:
isolation, neutrality, being a seer, and the state of being a non-agent.

children.text: tasmāt tatsaṃyogād acetanaṃ cetanāvad iva liṅgaṃ
children.translated_text: Therefore, from its conjunction with that, the unconscious subtle body appears as if conscious.
And likewise, when the <s>guṇas</s> are the agents, the indifferent one appears as if an agent.
For the sake of <s>puruṣa</s>'s seeing, and likewise for the sake of <s>pradhāna</s>'s isolation,

children.text: paṅgvandhavad ubhayor api saṃyogas tatkṛtaḥ sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there is conjunction of the two, like the lame and the blind; creation is produced from that.
From <s>prakṛti</s> comes <s>mahat</s>; from that, <s>ahaṃkāra</s>; from that, the group of sixteen.

children.text: tasmād api ṣoḍaśakāt pañcabhyaḥ pañca bhūtāni ||
children.translated_text: And from that group of sixteen, from the five, come the five gross elements.

children.text: adhyavasāyo buddhir dharmo jñānaṃ virāga aiśvaryam
children.translated_text: Ascertainment is intellect; virtue, knowledge, detachment, and lordly power
are its sāttvic form; the tāmasic form is the reverse of these.
Self-assertion is <s>ahaṃkāra</s>; from it proceeds a twofold creation:
the group of eleven and also the set of five subtle elements.
The sāttvic group of eleven proceeds from the modified <s>ahaṃkāra</s>.

children.text: bhūtādes tanmātraḥ sa tāmasas taijasād ubhayaṃ ||
children.translated_text: From the elemental source come the subtle elements; that is tāmasic, while from the fiery one come both.
The cognitive senses are those called eye, ear, nose, tongue, and skin.
Speech, hands, feet, anus, and genitals are called the organs of action.

children.text: ubhayātmakam atra manaḥ saṃkalpakam indriyaṃ ca sādharmyāt
children.translated_text: Here the mind is of both natures, an instrument of conception, and also a sense because of similarity.
Their plurality is due to particular transformations of the <s>guṇas</s> and to the distinctions among external objects.
With respect to sound and the other objects, the function of the five is held to be mere observation.
Speaking, taking, moving, excreting, and pleasure are the functions of the five others.
The function of the three, each with its own characteristic, is this uncommon function.
The common function of the instruments consists of the five vital airs, beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: yugapaccatuṣṭayasya tu vṛttiḥ kramaśaśca tasya nirdiṣṭā
children.translated_text: The function of the four together is simultaneous, but that one's function is also stated to be sequential.
Even so, with regard to the unseen as with the seen, the function of the three is preceded by that.
They each enter into their own respective function, caused by mutual intention.

children.text: puruṣārtha eva hetur na kenacit kāryate karaṇam ||
children.translated_text: The purpose of <s>puruṣa</s> alone is the cause; the instrument is not made to act by anyone.
The instrument is thirteenfold, performing appropriation, retention, and illumination.

children.text: kāryaṃ ca tasya daśadhāhāryaṃ dhāryam prakāśyaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: Its object is tenfold: to be appropriated, retained, and illuminated.

children.text: antaḥkaraṇaṃ trividhaṃ daśadhā bāhyaṃ trayasya viṣayākhyam
children.translated_text: The internal instrument is threefold; the external is tenfold and is called the object of the three.
The external instrument belongs to the present time; the internal instrument belongs to the three times.
Among these, the five cognitive senses have both specific and nonspecific objects.

children.text: vāg bhavati śabdaviṣayā śeṣāṇi tu pañcaviṣayāṇi ||
children.translated_text: Speech has sound as its object, while the remaining ones have the five objects.

children.text: sāntaḥkaraṇā buddhiḥ sarvaṃ viṣayam avagāhate yasmāt
children.translated_text: Because the intellect, together with the inner organ, apprehends every object,

children.text: tasmāt trividhaṃ karaṇaṃ dvāri dvārāṇi śeṣāṇi ||
children.translated_text: therefore the instrument is threefold: the principal doorway, while the rest are doors.
These particular modifications of the <s>guṇa</s>s, mutually distinct, are like lamps;
having illuminated the whole purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>, they present it to the intellect.

children.text: sarvam pratyupabhogaṃ yasmāt puruṣasya sādhayati buddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Because the intellect accomplishes every experience for <s>puruṣa</s>,

children.text: saiva ca viśinaṣṭi punaḥ pradhānapuruṣāntaraṃ sūkṣmam ||
children.translated_text: that very intellect again discriminates the subtle distinction between <s>pradhāna</s> and <s>puruṣa</s>.
The subtle elements are the undifferentiated particulars; from them come the five gross elements, and from the five,

children.text: ete smṛtā viśeṣāḥ śāntā ghorāśca mūḍhāśca ||
children.translated_text: these are remembered as differentiated particulars: peaceful, fierce, and dull.

children.text: sūkṣmā mātāpitṛjāḥ saha prabhūtais tridhā viśeṣāḥ syuḥ
children.translated_text: The differentiated particulars are threefold: subtle, born of mother and father, and together with the gross elements.
Of these, the subtle ones are permanent; those born of mother and father cease.
The <s>liṅga</s>, produced earlier, unattached, fixed, extending from <s>mahat</s> down to the subtle elements,
transmigrates without experience of its own, perfumed by dispositions.

children.text: citraṃ yathāśrayam ṛte sthāṇvādibhyo vinā yathā chāyā
children.translated_text: As a picture cannot exist without a support, and as a shadow cannot exist apart from a post and the like,

children.text: tadvad vināviśeṣair na tiṣṭhati nirāśrayaṃ liṅgam ||
children.translated_text: so too the <s>liṅga</s>, without differentiated particulars, does not stand without a support.
This <s>liṅga</s>, whose cause is the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>, through the connection of occasion and consequent,
and because of the pervasive power of <s>prakṛti</s>, assumes its various positions like an actor.
Dispositions such as <s>dharma</s> and the rest are seen as innate, natural, and derivative,
some depending on the instruments, and others, beginning with the embryo, depending on effects.

children.text: dharmeṇa gamanam ūrdhvaṃ gamanam adhastād bhavatyadharmeṇa
children.translated_text: By <s>dharma</s> there is movement upward; by <s>adharma</s> there is movement downward.
By knowledge there is release, while from the opposite, bondage is held to arise.

children.text: vairāgyāt prakṛtilayaḥ saṃsāro bhavati rājasād rāgāt
children.translated_text: From dispassion comes dissolution into <s>prakṛti</s>; from passion, which is rājasic, comes transmigration.
From lordly power there is non-obstruction; from its opposite there is the reverse of that.
This creation of mental states is called error, incapacity, satisfaction, and attainment;

children.text: guṇavaiṣamyavimardāt tasya ca bhedās tu pañcāśat ||
children.translated_text: and, because of the mutual pressure of the unequal <s>guṇa</s>s, its divisions are fifty.
There are five divisions of error, and because of defects in the instruments,
twenty-eight divisions of incapacity; satisfaction is ninefold and attainment eightfold.

children.text: bhedas tamaso 'ṣṭavidho mohasya ca daśavidho mahāmohaḥ
children.translated_text: The division of darkness is eightfold; delusion is eightfold, and great delusion is tenfold.
Gloom is eighteenfold, and so too blind gloom comes to be eighteenfold.
Incapacity is taught as the eleven injuries of the senses together with the injuries of the intellect.
The injuries of the intellect are seventeen, arising through the opposites of satisfaction and attainment.
The internal satisfactions are four, named nature, means, time, and fortune.
The external ones, from cessation regarding objects, are five; thus nine satisfactions are accepted.
Reasoning, instruction, study, the three removals of suffering, acquisition of friends,

children.text: dānaṃ ca siddhayo 'ṣṭau siddheḥ pūrvo 'ṅkuśas trividhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and giving are the eight attainments; before attainment there is the threefold goad.

children.text: na vinā bhāvair liṅgaṃ na vinā liṅgena bhāvanirvṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>liṅga</s> does not exist without dispositions, nor is there accomplishment of dispositions without the <s>liṅga</s>.

children.text: liṅgākhyo bhāvākhyas tasmād dvividhaḥ pravartate sargaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore creation proceeds in two forms: that called <s>liṅga</s> and that called dispositions.
The divine creation has eight alternatives, and the animal birth is fivefold.
The human is of one kind; in summary, this is the elemental creation.
Above, creation abounds in <s>sattva</s>; at the root it abounds in <s>tamas</s>.
In the middle it abounds in <s>rajas</s>, extending from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a clump of grass.

children.text: tatra jarāmaraṇakṛtaṃ duḥkham prāpnoti cetanaḥ puruṣaḥ
children.translated_text: There the conscious <s>puruṣa</s> experiences suffering caused by old age and death,

children.text: liṅgasya ā vinivṛttes tasmād duḥkhaṃ svabhāvena ||
children.translated_text: until the withdrawal of the <s>liṅga</s>; therefore suffering belongs to it by its very nature.
Thus this undertaking, produced by <s>prakṛti</s>, extending from <s>mahat</s> down to the differentiated gross elements,
is for the liberation of each <s>puruṣa</s>; though it is for another, it appears as if for itself.
As milk, though unconscious, flows for the sake of the calf's growth,
so the activity of <s>pradhāna</s> proceeds for the sake of the liberation of <s>puruṣa</s>.
As people engage in actions for the sake of ending eagerness,
so the unmanifest proceeds for the sake of the liberation of <s>puruṣa</s>.

children.text: raṅgasya darśayitvā nivartate nartakī yathā nṛtyāt
children.translated_text: As a dancer withdraws from dancing after showing herself to the audience,
so <s>prakṛti</s>, after revealing herself to <s>puruṣa</s>, withdraws.
Beneficial by many different means to the <s>puruṣa</s> who gives no benefit in return,
possessing the <s>guṇa</s>s for the sake of that one who is without <s>guṇa</s>s, she acts purposelessly for his purpose.

children.text: prakṛteḥ sukumārataraṃ na kiṃcid astīti me matir bhavati
children.translated_text: There is nothing more delicate than <s>prakṛti</s>; such is my thought,

children.text: yā dṛṣṭāsmīti punar na darśanam upaiti puruṣasya ||
children.translated_text: for once she has been seen, she does not again come into the sight of <s>puruṣa</s>, thinking, 'I have been seen.'

children.text: tasmān na badhyate addhā na mucyate nāpi saṃsarati kaścit
children.translated_text: Therefore no one is truly bound, nor released, nor does anyone transmigrate.

children.text: saṃsarati badhyate mucyate ca nānāśrayā prakṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is <s>prakṛti</s>, with many supports, that transmigrates, is bound, and is released.

children.text: rūpaiḥ saptabhir eva tu badhnātyātmānam ātmanā prakṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: With seven forms <s>prakṛti</s> binds herself by herself,
and that same <s>prakṛti</s>, for the purpose of <s>puruṣa</s>, releases herself by a single form.

children.text: evaṃ tattvābhyāsān nāsmi na me nāham ityapariśeṣam
children.translated_text: Thus, from practice of the principles, there arises completely the knowledge 'I am not, nothing is mine, I am not this,'
pure, isolated, and free from error because it is not mistaken.
Through that knowledge, <s>puruṣa</s>, standing comfortably like a spectator, sees <s>prakṛti</s>,

children.text: prakṛtim paśyati puruṣaḥ prekṣakavad avasthitaḥ susthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: whose productivity has ceased because her purpose is fulfilled, and who has withdrawn from the seven forms.
One, indifferent, thinks, 'She has been seen by me'; the other, having ceased, thinks, 'I have been seen.'

children.text: sati saṃyoge api tayoḥ prayojanaṃ nāsti sargasya ||
children.translated_text: Although the conjunction of the two still exists, there is no purpose for creation.
Through the attainment of right knowledge, when <s>dharma</s> and the rest no longer function as causes,
he remains, bearing the body by the force of impressions, like a wheel still turning.
When separation from the body has been reached, because the purpose has been fulfilled and <s>pradhāna</s> has withdrawn,
He obtains both kinds of <s>kaivalya</s> (isolation), the certain and the ultimate.
This secret knowledge of the human goal was fully declared by the supreme seer,
in which the persistence, origination, and dissolution of beings are considered.

children.text: etat pavitram agryam munir āsuraye anukampayā pradadau
children.translated_text: This foremost and purifying teaching the sage gave out of compassion to <s>Āsuri</s>.

children.text: āsurir api pañcaśikhāya tena bahudhākṛtaṃ tantram ||
children.translated_text: <s>Āsuri</s> too gave it to <s>Pañcaśikha</s>; by him the <s>tantra</s> (systematic doctrine) was made manifold.
Having come down through a succession of pupils, this doctrine was then, by <s>Īśvarakṛṣṇa</s>, in āryā verses,
condensed by one of noble understanding, after he had correctly understood the established doctrine.

children.text: saptatyāṃ kila ye arthās te arthāḥ kṛtsnasya ṣaṣṭitantrasya
children.translated_text: The meanings that are in the Seventy are indeed the meanings of the whole Ṣaṣṭitantra,
but without illustrative tales and also free from refutations of opposing doctrines.

children.text: tasmāt samāsadṛṣṭaṃ śāstram idaṃ nārthataśca parihīṇam
children.translated_text: Therefore this śāstra, seen in summary, is not deficient in meaning,
like the reflection of the great-bodied <s>tantra</s> transferred into a mirror.
